title: A client that hangs up is recorded as a 502 from the provider
foundBy: session agent, reading the claude-login cassettes in cs-sandbox while fixing VCR-021

evidence.verified: go test ./internal/proxy/ -run TestAnErrorForAClientThatLeftIsNotRecorded -count=1: PASS. Without the guard it fails with `recorded = 1`, over the same three log lines the cs-sandbox recording produced. Its two neighbours still pass: a hang-up mid-stream records what the client received, and a genuine transient is still recorded and flagged.

resolution: The tap now marks a status the reverse proxy's error handler wrote, and `record` declines to store one when the client had already gone. Both halves are needed. Without the client check, a genuine upstream failure the client did receive would stop being recorded. Without the marker, an interrupted stream would be dropped instead of kept. SPEC.md R28a carves the case out of R28, and the manual lists the warning.
details:
When a client disconnects mid-request, `ReverseProxy` calls its `ErrorHandler`. That handler writes a 502 `upstream_error` through the tap, and `record` stores it as a step of the session.

The 502 is cs-vcr's own. No provider sent it, and the client never saw it, because the client had already gone. The recording log says as much:

```
level=ERROR msg="upstream failed" err="context canceled"
level=WARN msg="recording a transient failure as a step of the session" status=502 cassette=claude-login-lent
level=INFO msg=recorded seq=2 cassette=claude-login-lent streaming=false events=0
```

Replay is then less faithful than the recording. The step is served to a client that is still alive and reading, so it receives an error the recorded session never delivered. R31 says why that matters: a Stainless SDK retries a 5xx, and the cassette holds no second copy of a request that was only asked once.

Two of cs-sandbox's committed fixtures carry one. `claude-login-lent` and `claude-login-shared` each end on a 502 whose body reads `{"error":{"type":"upstream_error","source":"cs-vcr"}}`. Claude Code prints its answer and exits while the session-title call is still in flight, so the race is reliable there rather than occasional. One recording run caught `opencode-fireworks-lent` the same way.

It is latent today. Those cassettes replay with every step served and nothing missed, because the agent exits before it can retry. A client that read the step and retried would miss.

The transient-failure branch is written for a provider having a bad moment, and that reasoning does not reach this case. `record` already computes `clientGone` from the request context, which is what separates the two. The neighbouring case is the `t.status == 0` branch, which declines to record when nothing reached the client at all.
